sections.title: Tree and foliage
sections.text: Tectona grandis, teak, is a large deciduous tree native from India to mainland Southeast Asia. It can reach about 40 m. Opposite leaves are very large—up to 75 cm long and about 45 cm wide—and hairy beneath. The plate shows the broad leaves and branching tree form.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Small white to pinkish flowers grow in large terminal panicles. The rounded, pale fruit is about 1.2–2 cm across and enclosed by an inflated, papery calyx; both fruit and calyx are represented on the plate.

sections.title: Uses and safety
sections.text: Teak is chiefly valued for its durable timber. The sources consulted do not verify a food use or species-specific toxicity for the pictured parts.
